h1: Portable roofing and siding brakes (aluminum brakes), 40″ to 12.5 ft
intro: A portable roofing and siding brake folds flashing, trim, drip edge and fascia on site: an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 to 15 minutes, that clamps 24 ga steel or 0.032″ aluminum coil, bends it to 180° and slits the coil with a roller knife. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: the ALB aluminum brakes, six models from 7.2 to 12.5 ft with a silicone insert in the bending beam for pre-painted coil and copper, a slitter on a track and a carrying stand; the BSM1550 and BSM3150 shear and brake machines that bend 22 ga over 61″ and 124″ and slit it over 59″ and 122″, with gas springs that lift the bending beam and carry the slitter head, on a mobile stand; and the BSM1016, BSM1220 and BSM2540 folding brakes with a slitter on a fold-away stand, 20 – 22 ga over 40 to 100″. The CD-24 coil dispenser feeds 24″ trim coil to the brake. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What do I need to bend roofing flashing on site?
faq.a: A portable roofing brake: the ALB brakes have an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 – 15 minutes, take 24 ga steel and 0.032″ aluminum over 7.2 – 12.5 ft, bend to 180° and slit the coil with a roller knife. Add the CD-24 dispenser for trim coil. For the shop, a box and pan brake or a magnetic brake does the same work in heavier gauges.

Long enough for the longest piece you make in one bend — 10 ft for fascia and drip edge is the common choice, 12.5 ft for commercial trim — and no longer, because the brake is carried: the 7.2 ft model weighs 132 lb, the 12.5 ft model about 220 lb. Longer pieces are made in two overlapping bends.

faq.q: Does the slitter come with the brake?
faq.a: Yes: a roller slitter on a track cuts the coil to width on the brake before folding, so a 24″ coil becomes drip edge, J-channel and fascia without a separate shear. Replacement cutting wheels are stocked in Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is a slitting brake, and what does a shear and brake machine add?
faq.a: A slitting brake has a slitter that runs along the clamping beam to cut a strip from the sheet before folding it — the tool for trim and flashing from coil. The BSM1016, BSM1220 and BSM2540 have a slitting device that comes off; the BSM1550 and BSM3150 shear and brake machines carry the slitter head on gas springs and slit 22 ga over 59″ and 122″, with a gas spring that lifts the bending beam, on a mobile stand.

No — the bending beam has a silicone insert and the clamping surfaces are smooth aluminum, made for pre-painted steel and aluminum coil and for copper. Keep the protective film on the coil for a flawless finish.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
